metaDescription: Six reversible sectionals with a movable chaise or ottoman compared on size, springs, storage, fabric and washing, from compact 78 in sets to a 147 in giant.
expertTake: The Chireca 80 in sectional is our top pick because it combines a reversible storage chaise with removable, machine-washable seat and back covers at a size that suits apartments. The Rlahery 78 in faux leather set is the value pick for a wipe-clean sofa with a sliding ottoman. Skip the category if you want a very large sectional with a fixed corner, because a reversible chaise gives up some of the structure of a fixed one.
introParagraphs: A reversible sectional lets you move the chaise or ottoman to the left or right, so one purchase can fit a corner on either side and survive a move to a different room. It is a simpler, cheaper idea than a full modular sofa, and it works best at small and medium sizes. The word reversible also gets used loosely, so it matters whether the chaise really flips or whether only a loose ottoman slides.

We evaluated each sectional from its published specifications and patterns in owner feedback, not from handling it. Listings often describe storage and cup holders at length and give little detail on frames, so we say what is missing. The lineup runs from compact sets for small rooms to a seven-seater so you can match the size to your room.

products.name: Chireca 80 in Convertible Sectional with Reversible Storage Chaise, Washable Covers

specList.label: Layout
specList.value: Small L-shaped, 3 seats, reversible storage chaise

specList.label: Covers
specList.value: Removable machine-washable seat and back covers

products.description:
The Chireca is an 80 in small L-shaped three-seater with a reversible storage chaise, and the listing says both the seat and the backrest cushions have removable, machine-washable covers for mud and fur. It is aimed at apartments, renters and pet owners. It is the most practical sofa in the lineup for a household that expects mess.

The tradeoff is size. At 80 in, three adults sit closely and the chaise is short, so it suits a small room more than a family room. Removable covers help only if you actually wash them, and machine washing a polyester cover can shrink it if the dryer is too hot. Compared with the Rlahery, it is washable but not wipe-clean, and the listing does not describe the frame.

Assemble the pieces and decide the chaise side before attaching the connectors. Wash covers on a gentle cycle and air dry. It suits a studio or a small living room where a sofa has to cope with pets and a move. Keep a spare set of connectors and the original instructions, since reassembling after a move is where small parts get lost.
products.bestFor: Apartments and renters with pets that want washable covers and a flip-side chaise.
pros: Seat and back covers are removable and machine washable per the listing
Reversible storage chaise adapts to a left or right corner
80 in size suits apartments, studios and small living rooms
Polyester upholstery wipes and washes better than natural fibers
cons: Compact 80 in body seats three adults closely
Listing gives little detail on the frame, so build quality is less certain

products.name: Rlahery 78 in L-Shaped Faux Leather Sectional with Sliding Storage Ottoman

specList.label: Extras
specList.value: Two cup holders built into the arms

products.description:
The Rlahery is a 78 in L-shaped sofa in beige faux leather with an ottoman that slides to either side and stores things inside, plus two cup holders built into the arms. The listing gives the size as about 77.99 in long and 28.74 in wide. It is the smallest sectional in the lineup and the easiest to wipe clean.

The tradeoff is the surface and the shape. Faux leather wipes easily but can crack or peel at the arms and seat edge after two to four years, and a sliding ottoman is a loose piece that can move when you do not want it to. Cup holders are convenient but fixed. Compared with the Chireca, it cleans faster but cannot be washed.

Keep it out of direct sun and away from heaters. Wipe it every couple of weeks and check the ottoman lid. It suits a small room or a home theater where a wipe-clean surface and storage matter. Place a felt pad under the ottoman's feet so that sliding it does not scratch a hard floor.
products.bestFor: Small rooms and home theaters that want a wipe-clean sofa with a sliding ottoman.

products.name: Hveodcid 85 in Chenille L-Sectional, Pocket Springs, Storage Ottoman, Cup Holders
products.description:
The Hveodcid is an 84.64 in L-shaped three-seater in dark blue chenille with high-density foam and pocket springs, a storage ottoman that can sit on either side and two cup holders. The listing says the springs maintain consistent support. It is the only sectional here that names pocket springs in the seat.

The tradeoff is that a dark blue chenille shows lint and pale pet hair, and chenille is dense and soft but holds hair. The ottoman is a loose piece, and the lid is a hinge that wears. Compared with the Rlahery, it is a little wider and has a sprung seat but cannot be wiped as quickly.

Expect a short assembly and a few days for the cushions to settle. Brush the chenille and keep the ottoman load light. It suits a small to medium living room where support and a rich color matter.
products.bestFor: Small to medium living rooms that want a sprung seat and a rich chenille color.

Cup holders and an 84.64 in body seat three comfortably

Ottoman lid and hinge are wear points over time

products.name: Shintenchi Modern L-Shaped Sectional with Storage Ottoman and Reversible Chaise
products.description:
The Shintenchi is a modern L-shaped three-seater with a reversible chaise, a storage ottoman and sleek minimalist lines. The listing says it suits small spaces and families alike. It is the cleanest-lined sofa in the lineup.

The tradeoff is documentation. The text we reviewed gives no dimensions, fabric content or frame details, so you must check the listing page. Minimalist sofas tend to have firm, shallow seats that suit upright sitting rather than lounging, and the storage lid adds a hinge. Compared with the Hveodcid, it offers a plainer look and less stated construction.

Measure the room and confirm the dimensions before ordering. Vacuum the seams weekly. It suits a modern living room where a quiet shape and hidden storage are the priority.

products.name: Belffin Convertible Corduroy Sectional with Reversible Corner Chaise, Curved Arms
products.description:
The Belffin is a convertible L-shaped sectional with a reversible corner chaise, curved sloped armrests and a thick, soft corduroy fabric. The listing calls it a space-maximizing solution. It is the only sectional in the lineup with curved arms and the softest corduroy.

The tradeoff is size information. The text we reviewed gives no dimensions, so the footprint needs checking, and corduroy hides crumbs while holding hair. Curved arms are comfortable but make the overall width harder to judge. Compared with the Chireca, it is more stylish and less documented on cleaning.

Choose the chaise side before connecting the pieces and vacuum the ribs weekly. It suits a living room where a soft texture and curved arms add character.

products.name: Ball and Cast 147 in L-Shaped Linen Sectional, 7 Seats, Reversible Chaise
products.description:
The Ball and Cast is a 147 in L-shaped sectional with seven seats, a reversible chaise, removable back cushions and a connect bar securing each module, in linen upholstery. The listing says the chaise can be placed on either side. It is the largest sectional in the lineup by a wide margin.

The tradeoff is room and delivery. A 147 in L needs a very large space, and a linen-style fabric wrinkles and shows stains. Removable back cushions help with cleaning and fluffing. Compared with the Chireca, it seats far more but cannot move easily, and the connect bars add stability to keep modules aligned.

Plan the delivery path and the room layout carefully, since the pieces are heavy. Vacuum the linen weave weekly. It suits a very large family room where seating for seven is needed. Because linen-style fabric wrinkles, a quick pass with a fabric steamer after cushion fluffing keeps it tidy.

buyingCriteria.explanation: On some sectionals the chaise itself flips from left to right, while on others only a loose ottoman slides. The Chireca and Ball and Cast describe a reversible chaise, and the Rlahery and Hveodcid use a sliding ottoman. Read the listing to see which one applies. A loose ottoman can wander during use, while a connected chaise stays put.

A chaise is held to the sofa by a connect bar, brackets or a frame joint. The Ball and Cast lists a connect bar on each module, and cloud-style sofas often have none. Weak connectors let sections drift on smooth floors. Check the connection after the first week, and again after any move. A bar that is not fully seated will let the chaise creep and open a gap that is hard to close with the sofa loaded.

The Chireca, Rlahery, Hveodcid and Shintenchi all include storage in the chaise or ottoman. A lid is a hinge, and hinges wear, squeak or trap fingers. Keep loads light and fingers clear. If you do not need storage, a simple reversible without it will age better.

The Hveodcid lists pocket springs and high-density foam, while most others list only foam. Springs hold shape longer under daily use. Foam-only seats soften in one to two years. Choose by how long you plan to keep it. Where the listing is silent on springs, assume foam over a simple base and expect the seat to soften in a year or two.

The Chireca has removable, washable covers, the Rlahery is wipe-clean faux leather, and the Belffin is corduroy that holds hair. Faux leather can peel, and washable covers can shrink. Pick by household, not by color. A cover you will never wash is wasted, and a surface that wipes clean suits a home with young children or a dog that sheds.

The Rlahery is 78 in long, the Chireca 80 in, the Hveodcid about 85 in and the Ball and Cast 147 in. Measure both walls of the corner and the door width. A reversible sectional only helps if both sides fit. Tape the footprint on the floor, and mark both chaise positions so that you can see how each would sit relative to the door, the radiator and the TV wall.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing specifications
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each sectional from the dimensions, chaise or ottoman design, springs and cover details stated on its Amazon listing. We did not handle any of them. The Chireca's 80 in width and the Ball and Cast's 147 in width are numbers we compare.

howWeEvaluated.title: On-topic filtering
howWeEvaluated.description: The topic search returned sleeper sectionals, which are covered in their own guide. We kept reversible sectionals without a pull-out bed. That left a lineup of six.

howWeEvaluated.title: What reversible means
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated true reversible chaises from sliding ottomans because the difference affects stability. Where a listing was vague, we say so. That is why the Chireca ranks first.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered recurring themes such as loose ottomans, drifting modules and faux leather peeling. We do not repeat ratings or counts. A pattern counted only when it matched the described construction.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: No listing here states a frame wood or a foam density. We say so plainly. Treat all of these as moderate-duty sectionals.

cards.label: Reversible chaise
cards.text: The Chireca, Belffin and Ball and Cast connect a chaise that can switch sides. It is more stable and looks like part of the sofa.

cards.label: Sliding ottoman
cards.text: The Rlahery and Hveodcid use a loose ottoman. It is simple and cheaper but can drift.

howToChoose.note: Choose a connected chaise for stability and a sliding ottoman for flexibility and lower cost.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A size that fits most rooms, covers you can wash, a chaise that flips and a box that fits a stairwell. Renters move often, so flexibility matters.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Chireca and Rlahery both suit renters, with the Chireca washable and the Rlahery wipe-clean.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a framed reversible sectional with a stated hardwood frame, hand-tied springs and a warranty. Those sit above these marketplace listings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The sectional is for a first apartment or a basement. A compact set like the Chireca covers that.

maintenance.why: Crumbs gather where the chaise meets the sofa. Use an upholstery brush.
Connect bars and brackets loosen. Tighten the Ball and Cast bars and check the Chireca chaise.
Follow the label and air dry. The Chireca covers are designed to be washed.
Body oils break down the coating. Use a damp cloth on the Rlahery.
Hinges wear. Keep heavy loads low in the ottoman or chaise.

faq.a: A sectional whose chaise or ottoman can be placed on the left or right. It lets one sofa fit either corner.

faq.q: Is a reversible chaise less sturdy?
faq.a: Not by design. The connection is what matters, and a connect bar or bracket keeps it stable.

faq.q: Can I switch the chaise later?
faq.a: Yes on true reversible sets, though it takes time and help. A sliding ottoman moves instantly.

faq.q: Is faux leather a good choice?
faq.a: It wipes clean but can crack or peel after a few years. Fabric is more breathable.
Most need some, from legs and connectors to a full frame. Check the listing.

faq.q: How do I choose the chaise side?
faq.a: Stand in the room and picture where the chaise ends. A reversible set lets you decide on delivery day.
